sections.title: Use of MeSH in Indexing
sections.extract: Source: <https://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/intro_indexing.html> · Last Reviewed: July 10, 2025 The MeSH vocabulary is primarily designed for use by NLM to index citations for journal articles in the MEDLINE database and to search the MEDLINE data using PubMed. sections.title: Preface
sections.extract: Source: <https://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/intro_preface.html> · Last Reviewed: July 9, 2025 1. Prefatory Remarks The Medical Subject Headings (MeSH®) thesaurus is a controlled vocabulary produced by the National Library of Medicine and used for indexing, cataloging, and searching for biomedical and health-related information and documents. MeSH includes the subject descriptors appearing in MEDLINE®/PubMed® and other NLM

sections.title: 1. Entry Terms
sections.extract: Entry terms, sometimes called "See cross-references", are synonyms, near-synonyms alternate forms, and other closely related terms in a MeSH record. Entry terms are not always strictly synonymous with the preferred term in the record or with each other. However, Entry terms are generally used interchangeably with the preferred term and are equivalent to the preferred term for purposes of cataloging, indexing and

sections.title: MeSH Tree Structures
sections.extract: Source: <https://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/intro_trees.html> · Last Reviewed: July 10, 2025 MeSH descriptors are organized in 16 categories: category A for anatomic terms, category B for organisms, C for diseases, D for drugs and chemicals, etc. Each category is further divided into subcategories. sections.extract: Source: <https://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/concept_structure.html> · Last Reviewed: July 14, 2025 Terms in a MeSH record which are strictly synonymous with each other are grouped in a category called a "Concept."
